message.content:
**DIRECTOR’S CUT: ANATOMY ARCADE LANDING PAGE (MOBILE 390x844)**

---

### (1) VISUAL INVENTORY (What’s Actually on Screen)

**Header Bar (Top 60px):**
*   **Logo Lockup:** Red rounded-square icon with white heart/medical cross inside. Text: **“ANATOMY”** (white, bold sans-serif) / **“ARCADE”** (cyan #00E5FF, same weight).
*   **Nav Controls:** Three circular dark buttons with thin white icons: Speaker/Volume, Gear/Settings, Hamburger Menu.

**Hero Content (Center-Left Aligned):**
*   **Eyebrow Tagline:** **“— THE HUMAN BODY. YOUR MISSION.”** (Cyan, all-caps, tracked-out, small font ~11-12px).
*   **Title Treatment:** **“ANATOMY”** (White, ultra-bold italic, massive ~48px) / **“ARCADE”** (Cyan, same weight/style, slight drop shadow or glow).
*   **Body Copy:** **“Become a nano-robot, enter the human body, and complete medical missions while learning how your body works.”** (White, regular weight, ~15px, left-aligned, max-width constrained).
*   **Floating Icon:** Small grey/white pill-shaped nano-bot icon hovering mid-sentence after “works.” (Looks like a loading spinner or decorative element—unclear).

**Primary CTA Stack:**
*   **Button 1 (Primary):** Full-width cyan rounded-pill button. Icon: Black play triangle (▶). Text: **“PLAY”** (Black, bold, all-caps). High contrast against cyan.
*   **Button 2 (Secondary):** Full-width transparent/dark-grey rounded-pill button with thin white border. Icon: Open book/document symbol. Text: **“MEET THE SCIENCE”** (White, all-caps, smaller than Play button).

**Footer Metadata:**
*   **Status Line:** **“MISSION 01 AVAILABLE — NO EXPERIENCE REQUIRED”** (Grey/white muted, all-caps, tiny ~10-11px, tracked out).

**Bottom Section (Partially Visible):**
*   **Section Header:** **“— CHOOSE YOUR MISSION”** (Cyan, matching eyebrow style).

**Background:**
*   Dark cinematic medical imagery—deep blues/blacks with red vascular/biological structures (veins? muscle fibers?) blurred or in low opacity. Bokeh effects suggesting depth inside a body.

---

### (2) THE AUTOPSY: EVERY VISUAL & UX FAILURE

**A. HIERARCHY & COMPOSITION (The “Where Do I Look?” Disaster)**
*   **The Title is Screaming at Me:** That “ANATOMY ARCADE” type is *way* too large for mobile. It’s eating 25% of the viewport height. On a 390px screen, that font size (~48-56px) forces the actual content (the value proposition) below the fold or crammed into a tiny space.
*   **Eyebrow vs. Title Clash:** The cyan eyebrow (“THE HUMAN BODY...”) and the cyan word “ARCADE” are competing for the exact same color attention. The eye bounces between them instead of flowing down.
*   **Dead Vertical Space:** Massive gap between the body copy and the PLAY button. That floating nano-bot icon looks like a layout error or a broken image loader, not an intentional design element. It creates a visual “hole.”
*   **Background Fighting Foreground:** Those red streaks on the right side? They’re bleeding into the text area without enough opacity reduction. It looks like compression artifacts or a glitched texture, not atmospheric depth.

**B. TYPOGRAPHY & READABILITY (Mobile-Safe? No.)**
*   **All-Caps Body Copy Sin:** “Become a nano-robot...” is sentence case (good), but everything else is SCREAMING CAPS. On mobile, sustained all-caps reduces readability by ~15-20% for scanning.
*   **Font Weight Confusion:** The logo uses a heavy bold, the title uses a heavy bold italic, the buttons use bold... there’s no typographic rhythm. It’s just “BIG” vs “small.”
*   **Line Height Issues:** The body copy looks tight. For medical/educational content (implied audience: students, casual gamers), you need 1.5–1.6 line-height for comfort. This looks like 1.3.
*   **Micro-Text Crime:** “MISSION 01 AVAILABLE...” is roughly 10px. That’s below Apple’s HIG minimum (11pt) and Google’s Material Design minimum (12sp). Unreadable for anyone over 25 or in daylight.

**C. COLOR & CONTRAST (Accessibility Nightmare)**
*   **Cyan on Dark Grey:** The “ARCADE” title and buttons use a neon cyan (#00FFFF approx). Against the dark background, this passes WCAG AA for large text but fails for normal text if it were smaller. However, the **real problem** is the **Play button**: black text on cyan. Depending on the exact hex, that’s likely failing contrast ratio for normal text (needs 4.5:1, probably hitting 3.8:1 here).
*   **Muted Grey on Dark:** The footer text (“NO EXPERIENCE REQUIRED”) is roughly #888 on #111. That’s contrast ratio of ~4.5:1—barely passing AA for normal text, but at that font size (10px), it effectively fails because small text requires higher contrast for legibility.
*   **Generic “Gamer” Palette:** Cyan + Magenta/Red + Black is the most overused “sci-fi medical” trope since 1995. It reads as “I bought this color scheme from a Unity asset store template.” Where’s the unique identity?

**D. BUTTONS & AFFORDANCES (Click Confusion)**
*   **Primary vs. Secondary Ambiguity:** The “MEET THE SCIENCE” button has a border but nearly identical background opacity to the page. It looks disabled or like a ghost button that forgot to load its background. The icon (book) is too small to recognize at a glance.
*   **Play Button Icon Misalignment:** That play triangle (▶) looks slightly off-center vertically or too large relative to the text. It’s creating uneven padding.
*   **Touch Target Sizes:** Buttons look tall enough (48px+), but the header icons (speaker, gear, menu) are packed into what looks like 40px circles. Fingers will miss. Standard is 44px minimum, 48px preferred.

**E. LAYOUT & SPACING (The “Slop” Factors)**
*   **No Grid Discipline:** The left margin for text is inconsistent. The logo aligns left, the headline aligns left, but the buttons are full-width (edge-to-edge with margins). The footer text has a different left indent again. It feels like three different designers worked on this in isolation.
*   **Clipping Risk:** “CHOOSE YOUR MISSION” at the bottom is cut off by the viewport edge with no breathing room. If this is the landing page fold, it’s teasing content you can’t see without scrolling, but there’s no visual cue (like a fade or arrow) indicating scrollability.
*   **The Floating Pill:** That grey icon between the copy and the button—is it a cursor? A character select hint? A loading state? It’s positioned in the “dead center” of negative space where the eye rests, making it a distraction rather than an enhancement.

**F. “AI Slop” & Generic Patterns (The Smell Test)**
*   **Stock Photo Background:** That blurry red/blue biological texture? It’s either a Midjourney generation of “inside human body dark cinematic” or a Shutterstock special. It lacks the specific aesthetic of a *nano-robot* view. Where are the cells? The mechanical elements? It’s generic “science darkness.”
*   **Template Typography:** That italic bold sans-serif for the title is literally the default “epic gaming” font choice. No custom lettering, no mechanical/medical flavor (no serifs suggesting precision, no monospace suggesting tech).
*   **Meaningless Tagline:** “THE HUMAN BODY. YOUR MISSION.” tells me nothing. It’s filler copy generated to sound “cinematic.” A real game would say “NAVIGATE THE BLOODSTREAM” or “DESTROY THE PATHOGEN.”

---

### (3) THE THREE HIGHEST-IMPACT FIXES (Do These Now)

**FIX #1: KILL THE GIANT TITLE & REBALANCE THE TYPE SCALE**
*   **Problem:** The title is consuming 25% of vertical real estate on mobile, pushing value props down and forcing micro-text elsewhere.
*   **Action:** Reduce “ANATOMY ARCADE” from ~52px to **32–36px max**. Increase body copy from ~15px to **16–17px** (mobile base). Increase the footer metadata from ~10px to **12px** (absolute minimum). 
*   **Why:** This single change recovers ~80px of vertical space, allows proper line-height (1.5) on the description, and makes the page scannable in under 2 seconds instead of looking like a banner ad.

**FIX #2: FIX THE CONTRAST & COLOR IDENTITY (Burn the Cyan)**
*   **Problem:** Neon cyan on black is the “default Unity sci-fi palette.” It causes eye strain and fails accessibility on the button text.
*   **Action:** Shift primary accent to a **high-luminance lime-green or amber-orange** (suggesting bioluminescence or medical warning) with **white text on the primary button**, not black. Ensure the primary button meets **WCAG AAA (7:1 ratio)**. Make the secondary button solid dark-grey (not transparent) with 50% opacity white border so it doesn’t look broken.
*   **Why:** Medical-thriller aesthetics work better with “toxic green” or “alarm orange” than “Tron legacy cyan.” White text on colored buttons is the industry standard for a reason—legibility.

**FIX #3: ESTABLISH A REAL GRID & KILL THE FLOATING DEBRIS**
*   **Problem:** Inconsistent left margins, mysterious floating icons, and dead space make this look like a wireframe that escaped Figma.
*   **Action:** Implement a **12px or 16px baseline grid**. Align all text to a strict **20px left margin** (or 24px). Remove the floating grey pill icon entirely—it adds zero information. Add **24px of bottom padding** before “CHOOSE YOUR MISSION” so it doesn’t look clipped. Ensure the background image has a **gradient overlay (black 0% → 80% opacity)** from top to bottom so text always has contrast regardless of what’s behind it.
*   **Why:** Right now, this looks like a student project. A strict grid + intentional overlay + removal of ambiguous elements signals “AAA production values” and “this UI was designed by humans, not prompted.”

**FINAL VERDICT:** This isn’t a landing page; it’s a movie poster pretending to be software. Shrink the ego (title), fix the accessibility (contrast), and respect the grid (spacing). Until then, it’s getting bounced back to the art team with a note saying “make it look like a game, not a PowerPoint template from 2008.”
